law_record.title: Right-of-way in crosswalk (1)(a)
law_record.text: Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.287 [NRS-484B-287-1c, NRS-484B-287-1d, NRS-484B-287-1e, LVMC-11-30-060-A, LVMC-11-30-060-B], 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B] and 484B.350 [LVMC-11-46-030]: When official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation, the driver of a vehicle shall yield the right-of-way, slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield, to a pedestrian crossing the highway within a crosswalk when the pedestrian is upon the half of the highway upon which the vehicle is traveling or onto which the vehicle is turning, or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the highway as to be in danger. As used in this section, “half of the highway” means all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction, and includes the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway.

activation_conditions: official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation at the crossing
a pedestrian is crossing the highway within a crosswalk
the pedestrian is on the half of the highway the subject travels on or is turning onto, or is approaching so closely from the other half as to be in danger
exceptions: the crossing rules the text cites for pedestrians outside crosswalks, the white-cane rule, and the school-crossing rule govern instead where they apply
residue: 'in danger' is a judgement element bounding the approach from the far half
summary.subject: driver

timing_requirements.requirement: the yield is owed while the pedestrian is in the protected half and until the conflict passes
the pedestrian completes the crossing of the subject's path first
